summary: kmf-i18n ships a native addon that exfiltrates host identifiers to a hardcoded bare IP on require
details: The npm package kmf-i18n@100.100.101 is a functionless stub whose entire payload is a Linux-only native addon shipped at prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node. The main entry index.js exports an empty object and wraps a try/catch require of that addon, so loading the package via require("kmf-i18n") executes the native binary. On N-API module registration the addon reads the hostname (gethostname), the local user via getpwuid, and the npm_package_name and npm_config_registry environment variables, and POSTs them in cleartext HTTP to the hardcoded bare IP 64.181.165.115 at path /dc (format string 'h=%.60s&u=%.30s&p=%.50s&r=%.100s'). The addon imports socket/connect/send and fork. The manifest describes the package as 'Frontend utilities', but no JavaScript implementation is present and no library API is exported — the beacon is the only behavior. The combination of a hardcoded bare-IP non-first-party destination, plaintext HTTP, swallowed require errors concealing the native call, and an empty JS surface is a load-time exfiltration beacon disclosing installer identity and registry configuration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
